newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Quotas/ESAF to top IMF annual meeting agenda.
newsitem.headline: Quotas/ESAF to top IMF annual meeting agenda.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will seek to boost its capital base substantially and make its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility permanent at the annual IMF-World Bank meeting in September, IMF officials said.

"The main issue is the Fund's quotas. The Fund is a quota-based institution and it needs to expand its basic core financial base," David Goldsbrough, senior advisor, Asia and Pacific Department of the IMF told Reuters.
"Making ESAF permanent will also be very high on the agenda," Goldsbrough added at a one-day IMF-Hong Kong Monetary Authority conference on Asian financial integration.
ESAF lends money at virtually no interest charge to the world's poorest nations.

IMF managing director Michel Camdessus has called for a doubling to US$440 billion of the IMF's capital base through a quota increase. He told the conference on Friday that the quota increase "will need to be substantial".
"The Fund is a cooperative institution based on quotas and its strength and credibility depend on maintaining its quota strength," Camdessus said.
The Fund has seen its coffers depleted in recent years by huge loans to Mexico and Russia.
Hubert Neiss, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, said capital account liberalisation would also be among the September meeting's top issues.

Hong Kong is set to host the September IMF/World Bank meeting, the first major international extravaganza planned after the territory reverts to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30. -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6345
